Name: No More Tortillas (Lavash Power)
Author: LilietBorodina
Description:
[img]https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f3/Lavash%2C_Temple_Fortune%2C_London_%284444275978%29.jpg/250px-Lavash%2C_Temple_Fortune%2C_London_%284444275978%29.jpg[/img]

[url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lavash]From: Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia[/url]

[b]Lavash[/b] ([url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Armenian_language]Armenian[/url]: լավաշ; [url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Persian_language]Persian[/url]: نان لواش) is a thin [url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flatbread]flatbread[/url][url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lavash#cite_note-9][9][/url] usually [url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leavened]leavened[/url], traditionally baked in a [url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tandoor]tandoor[/url] ([i]tonir[/i] or [i]tanoor[/i]) or on a [i][url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sajj]sajj[/url][/i], and common to the cuisines of [url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Caucasus]South Caucasus[/url], [url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Asia]West Asia[/url], and the areas surrounding the [url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caspian_Sea]Caspian Sea[/url].[url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lavash#cite_note-10][10][/url][url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lavash#cite_note-Marks_2010_-_Lavash-11][11][/url][url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lavash#cite_note-12][12][/url] Lavash is one of the most widespread types of bread in [url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Armenia]Armenia[/url], [url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Azerbaijan]Azerbaijan[/url], [url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iran]Iran[/url], and [url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turkey]Turkey[/url].[url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lavash#cite_note-13][13][/url] The traditional recipe can be adapted to the modern kitchen by using a [url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Griddle]griddle[/url] or [url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wok]wok[/url] instead of the [i]tonir[/i].[url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lavash#cite_note-14][14][/url]
In 2014, "Lavash, the preparation, meaning and appearance of traditional bread as an expression of culture in Armenia" was inscribed
in the [url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UNESCO_Intangible_Cultural_Heritage_Lists]UNESCO Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity[/url].[url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lavash#cite_note-unesco-15][15][/url] In 2016, the making and sharing of flatbread (lavash, katyrma, jupka or [url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saj_bread]yufka[/url]) in communities of Azerbaijan, Iran, [url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kazakhstan]Kazakhstan[/url], [url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kyrgyzstan]Kyrgyzstan[/url], and Turkey was inscribed on the list as well.[url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lavash#cite_note-unesco2-16][16][/url] Lavash is similar to [i]yufka[/i], but in [url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turkish_cuisine]Turkish cuisine[/url] lavash ([i]lavaş[/i]) is prepared with a yeast dough while [i]yufka[/i] is typically unleavened.[url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lavash#cite_note-17][17][/url]
